extraction.name: MVBench: A Comprehensive Multi-modal Video Understanding Benchmark
extraction.description: MVBench is a comprehensive multi-modal video understanding benchmark covering 20 challenging video tasks that cannot be effectively solved with a single frame. The benchmark systematically evaluates temporal understanding capabilities of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs) through multiple-choice question answering across tasks ranging from action recognition to episodic reasoning.
extraction.creator: Kunchang Li, Yali Wang, Yinan He, Yizhuo Li, Yi Wang, Yi Liu, Zun Wang, Jilan Xu, Guo Chen, Ping Luo, Limin Wang, Yu Qiao
extraction.publisher: Shanghai AI Laboratory, Shenzhen Institute of Advanced Technology Chinese Academy of Sciences, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, The University of Hong Kong, Fudan University, State Key Laboratory for Novel Software Technology Nanjing University
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Videos are selected from 11 existing public video benchmarks including STAR, PAXION, Moments in Time V1, FunQA, CLEVRER, Perception Test, Charades-STA, MoVQA, NTU RGB+D, VLN-CE and TVQA. Data filtration is performed based on video diversity (covering first-person to third-person perspectives, indoor to outdoor environments), temporal sensitivity (selecting videos with intermediate duration primarily ranging from 5s to 35s), and question difficulty (balancing complexity by excluding overly simple or complex questions).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Videos collected from 11 public video datasets: STAR (real-world indoor third-person), PAXION (real-world and simulated indoor/outdoor third-person), Moments in Time V1 (real-world and simulated indoor/outdoor third-person), FunQA (real-world indoor/outdoor third-person), CLEVRER (simulated indoor), Perception Test (real-world indoor first and third-person), Charades-STA (real-world indoor third-person), MoVQA (real-world indoor/outdoor third-person), NTU RGB+D (real-world indoor third-person), VLN-CE (simulated indoor first-person), and TVQA (real-world indoor/outdoor third-person).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For STAR dataset, the challenge was enhanced by randomly shifting the start or end points of video clips to increase the complexity of localizing specific events. For CLEVRER dataset, questions requiring more than 10 conditions for describing specific events were excluded to decrease QA difficulty. Videos with intermediate duration (primarily 5s to 35s) were selected, eliminating short clips with minimal movement and extremely long videos with overly complicated contexts.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data filtration based on three criteria: (1) Video Diversity: selecting videos from 11 datasets covering broad spectrum of domains and scenes; (2) Temporal Sensitivity: eliminating short clips and extremely long videos, selecting intermediate duration videos (5s to 35s); (3) Question Difficulty: balancing difficulty by excluding overly simple or complex questions. Videos are processed using TSN sampling. For evaluation, 16-frame videos with resolution 224×224 are used as input.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Multiple-choice QAs are automatically generated from existing video annotations using two methods: (1) Template-Based Construction: option candidates constructed directly from ground truth annotations (e.g., for Action Antonym task, candidates contain correct action, its opposite action, and a not-sure choice); (2) LLM-Based Generation: ChatGPT used to generate questions based on task definitions and convert open-ended QAs into multiple-choice format. For each question, 3 to 5 answer options are randomly sampled from available candidates, and option order is shuffled. LLM is used to ensure all answer options have similar and reasonable text lengths. Ultimately, 200 multiple-choice QA pairs are produced for each of the 20 temporal understanding tasks.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Answer options are randomly sampled and shuffled to strengthen evaluation robustness. LLM is used to guarantee that all answer options of a question are of similar and reasonable lengths to prevent answer leakage where longer options tend to be correct. A detailed system prompt encourages MLLMs to carefully scrutinize video content by paying attention to actions, poses of persons, and details and movements of objects. An answer prompt 'Best Option: (' is used to guide MLLMs for option generation, achieving 100% rate in option extraction.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: ChatGPT for question generation and QA conversion, UMT-L/16 for action predictions in Fine-grained Action task
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Current MLLMs have difficulty generalizing to localization and counting tasks in the absence of related tuning data. Models perform poorly on position-related tasks, with performances analogous to random guessing. For counting and character-related tasks, models perform similarly or worse than text-only baselines without videos. Models encounter difficulties with complex egocentric navigation and episode reasoning. Visual information alone may not be sufficient for some tasks; inclusion of other modalities such as depth and audio could prove beneficial.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs) for temporal video understanding capabilities. The benchmark is designed to assess 20 challenging video tasks across categories including Action (Action Sequence, Action Prediction, Action Antonym, Fine-grained Action, Unexpected Action), Object (Object Existence, Object Interaction, Object Shuffle), Position (Moving Direction, Action Localization), Scene (Scene Transition), Count (Action Count, Moving Count), Attribute (Moving Attribute, State Change), Pose (Fine-grained Pose), Character (Character Order), and Cognition (Egocentric Navigation, Episodic Reasoning, Counterfactual Inference). Usage guidelines emphasize evaluation of temporal understanding that cannot be effectively solved with a single frame.
